title: Platform fit and safe areas
purpose: Checks aspect, resolution, frame rate, encoding, loudness, safe-area use and sound-off readability, and records them as render settings and constraints.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: A7 stream facts; F1 frames with a safe-area overlay drawn by drawbox; F12 black frames; F6 YAVG series for flashes.
pitfalls: Stating platform limits from memory; check current platform documentation and cite it, or say 'not checked'
Treating a safe-area template from one app as universal
Ignoring that the source may be a re-encode

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.text: one technique description, at most 300 characters, no copied content
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F6: Per-frame colour statistics (YMIN, YAVG, YMAX, SATAVG, HUEMED, UAVG, VAVG): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=$WORK/stats.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.F12: Black frames: ffmpeg -i "$SRC" -vf "blackdetect=d=0.05:pix_th=0.10" -an -f null - 2>&1 | grep black_

questions.question: What are the resolution and display aspect ratio?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills source.resolution and visual.aspect.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.source.width and height (video_re_probe_metadata); check A7 for sample_aspect_ratio and rotation side data.
questions.challenge: A rotation tag can swap width and height; confirm on an F1 frame.

questions.question: What is the average frame rate in frames per second?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills source.fps and the render frame rate.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.source.fps (avg_frame_rate); compare with r_frame_rate in A7 and report both in the note.
questions.challenge: Different r_frame_rate and avg_frame_rate indicate variable frame rate; say so.

questions.question: Which duration band does the video fit, and which platform limits should be checked against current platform documentation?
questions.why_it_matters: Records duration constraints without stating platform limits from memory.
questions.how_to_answer: Report source.duration_s; list platforms the user targets and mark each limit 'check current docs' unless a citation is supplied in the run.
questions.challenge: Any platform limit stated without a dated source is rejected.

questions.question: Which safe-area violations did the probe report, and are they real?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills visual.safe_area_respected.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.safe_area.violations (video_re_safe_area_probe); inspect F1 frames at 3 violation times with a drawbox overlay of the template.
questions.challenge: Name the template the probe used; violations from watermark regions are not format violations.

questions.question: Is any text placed in the bottom 20% of the frame?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a placement constraint (many vertical apps draw captions and controls there).
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.text_regions[] with bbox bottom beyond 0.8 x height.
questions.challenge: Treat the 20% figure as a working template, not a platform specification.

questions.question: Is any text placed in the right-hand 15% of the frame?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a placement constraint for side action buttons.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.text_regions[] with bbox right edge beyond 0.85 x width.
questions.challenge: Same caveat as 005.

questions.question: Is the top 10% kept free of important content?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a top margin constraint.
questions.how_to_answer: text_regions and subject positions in the top band.
questions.challenge: Report what occupies the band if anything.

questions.question: Would the important content survive a centre crop to 4:5 and to 1:1?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether variants can be re-framed for other placements.
questions.how_to_answer: Overlay 4:5 and 1:1 centre boxes on 5 F1 frames (drawbox); check title, captions and subject.
questions.challenge: Report per frame.

questions.question: Are there letterbox or pillarbox bars?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags a framing error to avoid.
questions.how_to_answer: ffmpeg cropdetect over 10 s: ffmpeg -i SRC -vf cropdetect -t 10 -f null - 2>&1 | tail -3.
questions.challenge: Dark content can trigger cropdetect; check on F1.

questions.question: What are the video codec, profile, pixel format and bitrate?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills render video settings.
questions.how_to_answer: A7 stream and format fields.
questions.challenge: Copy exactly from ffprobe.

questions.question: How does integrated loudness compare with common streaming normalisation targets (difference in LU from a target the run specifies)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the loudness target for the render.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.audio.integrated_lufs minus the target given in the run parameters; if none, report the value only.
questions.challenge: Do not assert a platform's target from memory; cite or omit.

questions.question: Are platform UI elements, usernames or watermarks burned into the frames?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags re-uploads and fills source.platform as an observation; such marks never enter variants.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops of corners and edges at 3 times.
questions.challenge: Do not name individuals; record the kind of mark and its position.

questions.question: Are captions burned in so the video can be followed with sound off?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills burned_in for sound-off viewing.
questions.how_to_answer: F1 frames during speech.
questions.challenge: Check 5 speech moments.

questions.question: What share of speech time has matching on-screen text (sound-off coverage)?
questions.why_it_matters: Measures sound-off readability.
questions.how_to_answer: Speech segments overlapped by caption-area text regions / speech time.
questions.challenge: Text regions are sampled; state the sampling interval.

questions.question: Are there interlacing or combing artefacts?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags a source quality issue.
questions.how_to_answer: ffmpeg idet filter over 500 frames: ffmpeg -i SRC -vf idet -frames:v 500 -an -f null - 2>&1 | grep 'Multi frame'.
questions.challenge: Report the counts.

questions.question: What colour primaries, transfer and range are tagged?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills render colour tags.
questions.how_to_answer: A7: color_space, color_transfer, color_primaries, color_range.
questions.challenge: Untagged streams must be reported as untagged, not as bt709.

questions.question: What are the audio channel layout and sample rate?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills render audio settings.
questions.how_to_answer: A7 audio stream.
questions.challenge: Copy exactly.

questions.question: Is the frame rate variable?
questions.why_it_matters: Variable frame rate affects frame-accurate measurements and renders.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A7 r_frame_rate and avg_frame_rate; inspect pts deltas with ffprobe -show_frames on 100 frames.
questions.challenge: Report min and max frame durations.

questions.question: What are the minimum text margins in px at the source resolution?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills a safe box for the render template.
questions.how_to_answer: Min distance from text bboxes to each edge.
questions.challenge: Exclude watermarks.

questions.question: What changes would a 16:9 version need (re-layout, pillarbox, side panels)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a reframing plan for other aspects.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect layout on F1 frames; propose a layout that keeps title, captions and subject; method inferred.
questions.challenge: Must not require source footage.

questions.question: Are handles, hashtags or account names overlaid as part of the design?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a handle slot (filled with the new channel's own handle) or rules it out.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops; describe placement and style only.
questions.challenge: Never copy the handle.

questions.question: Are there black frames at the start, the end, or anywhere else?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags autoplay and thumbnail problems.
questions.how_to_answer: F12 blackdetect.
questions.challenge: Report all segments.

questions.question: How many large luminance flashes per second occur at most (three per second is the WCAG 2.3.1 general flash threshold)?
questions.why_it_matters: An accessibility check; renders should stay under the threshold.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG per frame; count opposing changes above about 10% of full range within any 1 s window. This is a screening estimate, not a certified photosensitivity test.
questions.challenge: Small-area flashes count differently under WCAG; mark the result as a screening estimate.

questions.question: How tall is caption text in pixels at 1080 px width (scaled from the source)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a concrete size for phone legibility.
questions.how_to_answer: Cap height (typography lens) scaled to a 1080-wide frame.
questions.challenge: Recompute the scaling.

questions.question: Which platform parameters should a new video set (target platforms, aspect, fps, safe box, target loudness)?
questions.why_it_matters: Feeds the parameteriser.
questions.challenge: Each parameter needs derived_from.

questions.question: Write the safe-box rule for text and key subjects as fractions of width and height.
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a placement constraint.
questions.how_to_answer: From 005-007 and 019, for example 'text inside x 0.06-0.85, y 0.10-0.80'.
questions.challenge: Check the source's own text against the rule and report violations.

questions.question: Is the file a re-encode of an earlier upload (double compression signs, burned UI, odd bitrate)?
questions.why_it_matters: Calibrates trust in colour, sharpness and audio measurements.
questions.how_to_answer: A7 encoder tags, F3 crops for blocking, burned-in UI from 012; method inferred.
questions.challenge: Encoder tags can be stripped; low confidence unless two cues agree.

questions.question: What keyframe (GOP) interval does the file use?
questions.why_it_matters: Informs render settings and seek accuracy of measurements.
questions.how_to_answer: ffprobe -select_streams v -skip_frame nokey -show_entries frame=pts_time -of csv SRC | head -20; median interval.
questions.challenge: Report the first 10 keyframe times.

questions.question: Is the audio present for the whole duration, or shorter or longer than the video?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags sync and duration problems.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare audio and video stream durations in A7.
questions.challenge: Report both durations.

questions.question: Does the first frame contain the title and subject so a paused autoplay frame still communicates the topic?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a first-frame content rule.
questions.how_to_answer: F1 at 0.0 s.
questions.challenge: Cross-check with hook_first_seconds-001 and -019.
